 "description": "Examines foundational practices and theory in expressive therapies. Considers the ways that expressive therapies are used in clinical and community-based settings as a tool to improve well-being and mental health. Explores expressive modalities such as the visual arts, performing arts, movement, music, and creative writing. Special attention is given to contemporary topics including trauma, human development, and social and economic inequalities. Considers the application of expressive therapies in different settings, such as schools, hospitals, residential programs, and prisons.",
